title: Fixed Priority and Round-Robin Contention
description: The protocol defines request, grant, and legal handover; the SoC chooses the arbitration policy. Compare latency and fairness for the same sustained CPU and DMA requests.

phases.name: CPU service
phases.description: With CPU configured above DMA, a continuously requesting CPU can retain service across successive arbitration decisions.

phases.name: Waiting
phases.description: DMA remains eligible but waits while the higher-priority CPU keeps requesting. A real design needs a starvation policy or bounded-latency requirement.

phases.name: DMA service
phases.description: DMA is granted only after CPU releases its request in this example.

phases.name: CPU service
phases.description: CPU wins the first arbitration decision.

phases.name: Waiting
phases.description: CPU remains requesting while the rotating policy gives DMA an opportunity.

phases.name: CPU service
phases.description: CPU returns after DMA's service window. Exact quantum and eligibility rules are implementation-defined.

phases.name: Waiting
phases.description: DMA waits for the current owner's legal handover boundary.

phases.name: DMA service
phases.description: The rotating policy services DMA even though CPU is still requesting, preventing indefinite starvation in this example.
